scope: New collection_preferences rule only; existing application rules are unchanged and not comprehensively re-audited.
summary: The new shared household override path validates bounded canonical IDs, a strict two-field document, boolean visibility and a server timestamp on every create/update. Access uses existing trusted authentication plus stored household membership. Reset requires the same membership and deletes the override. Anonymous demo clients cannot persist preferences.

validation.sdkTests: 21 service/hook tests passed, including false versus absent, delayed initialization, stale household reads/errors, template isolation and failed writes.
validation.rulesCompilation: Official Firebase rules compilation dry run passed; no release or rules deployment was performed.
validation.emulatorResult: All passed against the actual Firestore rules evaluator. No production household records were read or written by these tests.

attackChecks: A trusted nonmember cannot read or overwrite another household's preference.
An untrusted authenticated client cannot read, create or delete preferences.
A member cannot write through a different household path.
An anonymous template visitor cannot persist preferences.
Create rejects missing fields, nonboolean visibility, extra privilege fields and forged historical timestamps.
Create rejects malformed and oversized provider/collection identities.
A valid create does not let a later update bypass strict schema validation.
The household collection query is permitted for actual members.
Two trusted household members can read and change the same canonical override.
Member deletion restores absence, distinct from explicit false.
releaseNotes: Prototype Security Rules scoped to the existing trusted membership model. Review and verify them before broadly sharing the app. This revision performs no production deployment. Include the new collection_preferences rules in the reviewed future release before enabling connected-household Show/Hide writes; otherwise the existing default-deny rules reject that path.
